entries.0766cf8fc5f9ef2d: In thermal power generation, toward equipment upgrades to the latest high-efficiency combined-cycle units, the company is advancing an equipment renewal plan at the Nanko Power Station and evaluating business viability at the Himeji Daiichi Power Station. The Ako Power Station, Unit 2 of the Gobo Power Station, and the Kansai International Airport Energy Center were decommissioned in consideration of aging equipment and changes in the business environment. In hydrogen, the company conducted a demonstration of hydrogen co-firing power generation at the Himeji Daini Power Station and, in June 2025, achieved a co-firing ratio of 30% (by volume), the first in Japan for a commercial large gas turbine.

entries.1af1154ea8f5eb03: This is a reportable segment that delivers electricity safely and stably from a neutral and impartial standpoint. It operates the power grid and plans and carries out construction of transmission, substation and distribution facilities. In April 2020, the general transmission and distribution business operated by The Kansai Electric Power Company, Incorporated was transferred to Kansai Transmission and Distribution, Inc. through a company split. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥386,221 million, a decrease of ¥2,899 million (−0.7%) from the previous fiscal year. The reason was a decrease in inter-area and other companies' electricity sales revenue associated with supply-demand adjustment transactions. Including intersegment internal revenue of ¥671,524 million, the total was ¥1,057,746 million, and transactions within the group account for a large share. Based on its five-year business plan for fiscal 2023 to 2027, set under the transmission charge system, Kansai Transmission and Distribution, Inc. is renewing aged facilities and advancing the next-generation upgrade of its power network to support decarbonization and enhanced resilience.

entries.4baf76e151e08c4b: In hydropower, Unit 3 of the Kasagi Power Station, whose maximum output was increased through equipment renewal, began operation. In offshore wind, the company is conducting on-site surveys off Yuza Town, Yamagata Prefecture, and in January 2026, the Goto Offshore Wind Farm off Goto City, Nagasaki Prefecture, began operation. The company is expanding its business in Japan and overseas, including participation in storage station businesses such as grid-connected battery storage, the Windanker offshore wind power project in Germany, and an investment in Simply Blue Energy in Ireland.
entries.50272766e62506eb: This is a reportable segment that provides new value through diverse solutions, such as electricity, gas and utility services. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥3,261,386 million, the largest of the four reportable segments, and it decreased by ¥279,392 million (−7.9%) from the previous fiscal year. The reason was a decrease in electricity sales revenue. Total electricity sold was 152.3 billion kWh, a decrease of 2.4% from the previous fiscal year. In addition, in line with the Kansai Electric Power Group Management Plan 2026 formulated in April 2026, the Business Solution Business, which had previously been classified under the Life and Business Solutions Business, will move to this segment from the next consolidated fiscal year. Meanwhile, the hyperscale data center business that had been included in this segment will move to the Information and Telecommunications Business.
entries.505ab7c2573a22b7: For residential customers, in addition to menus for all-electric homes, the company offers products such as the “Hapi e Set,” which bundles lease fees for Eco Cute water heaters, solar power systems and storage battery equipment with electricity charges up to a certain volume. The company has also advanced proposals bundling electricity and gas, and as of the end of the fiscal year, the number of Kanden Gas contracts was approximately 1.63 million. For corporate customers, the company offers the “Zero Carbon Package,” which supports decarbonization from plan development through implementation. Its core company, Kanden Energy Solution Co., Ltd., provides utility services nationwide.
entries.5f81e122efae22b4: This is a reportable segment that, in addition to comprehensive real estate business including leasing, sale and management of properties and leisure, develops services such as call center operations and medical and healthcare services that realize safe, comfortable and convenient lives and businesses for customers. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥186,833 million, an increase of ¥3,206 million (+1.7%) from the previous fiscal year. The reason was an increase in rental income from residential and office buildings in the leasing business of Kanden Realty & Development Co., Ltd. Its core company, Kanden Realty & Development Co., Ltd., saw strong condominium sales in its residential sales business, centered on the Kansai region and the Tokyo metropolitan area. In February 2026, Shieria Tower Nakanoshima was completed, and in October 2025, Kanden Fudosan Kayabacho Building, its first compact office, was completed. The company is also involved in residential development and leasing businesses in the United States, Australia and elsewhere. In addition, in line with the formulation of the Kansai Electric Power Group Management Plan 2026 in April 2026, from the next consolidated fiscal year this segment will be renamed the Real Estate Business, and the Business Solution Business will move to the Energy Business.
entries.604b29f0f6d831a7: The group consists of the company and 216 affiliated companies (109 [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiaries]], 9 unconsolidated subsidiaries and 98 affiliates, as of March 31, 2026). In April 2020, the company transferred its general transmission and distribution business to Kansai Transmission and Distribution, Inc. through a company split.
entries.60e45bb0401e036f: The company generates power using nuclear, thermal, hydro and renewable energy, and sells electricity and gas. Kanden Energy Solution and others provide utility services, Kansai Transmission and Distribution handles transmission and distribution, Optage handles information and communications such as 'eo Hikari' and 'mineo', and Kanden Real Estate Development handles real estate leasing and sales.
entries.652d1eefdc71ae27: Consolidated revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥4,056,638 million, down ¥280,473 million (6.5%) from the previous year. The reason was a decrease in electricity sales revenue. Revenue from external customers by [[term:segment|reportable segment]] was ¥3,261,386 million for the Energy Business, ¥386,221 million for the Transmission and Distribution Business, ¥222,196 million for the Information and Communications Business and ¥186,833 million for the Living and Business Solutions Business, with the Energy Business the largest.

entries.870b5cfd9ffe2109: This is a reportable segment that provides comprehensive information and telecommunications services. In addition to offering three FTTH-based services (optical internet, optical telephone and optical TV) under the “eo Hikari” brand across the Kansai region, the segment runs the mobile business “mineo” for nationwide customers and a corporate solutions business. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥222,196 million, a decrease of ¥1,388 million (−0.6%) from the previous fiscal year. Corporate services and other offerings of Optage Inc. increased, but the exclusion of a consolidated subsidiary from the scope of consolidation weighed on results. Its core company, Optage Inc., provides “eo Hikari” to approximately 1.7 million customers and “mineo” to approximately 1.41 million customers. In January 2026, it opened the urban data center “Sonezaki Data Center.” Kanden Systems Co., Ltd. is responsible for system development for the group. Kansai Denryoku CyrusOne Co., Ltd., which was established with CyrusOne, a US company, began construction of the first project of its hyperscale data center business in Seika Town, Kyoto Prefecture, in August 2025, and aims to begin operations within fiscal 2027. This business was classified under the Energy Business in the segment notes for the fiscal year ended March 2026, but from the next consolidated fiscal year it will be classified under the Information and Telecommunications Business.
